One of Canada’s Most Trusted Investment Brands.

At Picton Mahoney Asset Management (PICTON Investments),
being alternative isn’t just what we do—it’s who we are.

Founded by industry pioneer David Picton, we’ve spent 20 years challenging conventional wisdom and redefining the investing landscape. As one of Canada’s most trusted investment brands, we are proudly independent—privately run, 100% employee-owned, and deeply committed to delivering results for our clients.

Thinking Alternatively is in Our DNA

With a team of 233 bold thinkers—one-third dedicated solely to investment management—we are specialists, not generalists. Managing over $19.9 billion (September 30, 2026) for institutional and retail clients, we navigate markets with conviction, resilience, and a forward-thinking approach.

We’re more than investors — we’re innovators. We challenge traditional investment mindsets, constantly pushing the boundaries to achieve our mission: To bring greater certainty to investors.

Our success is built on four guiding principles:

Treat investors’ money like our own.
Redefine the way investors invest.
Be human—always approachable.
Succeed together, one investment at a time.

These aren’t just words—they define how we think, how we invest, and how we work.

Now, we’re entering our next chapter. We’re transforming our brand and reshaping the way the world invests. If you think alternatively, embrace an entrepreneurial spirit, and thrive in a dynamic, bureaucracy-free environment, join us and be part of what’s next.

Thriving in Our Entrepreneurial Culture

At PICTON Investments
, you’ll thrive in our creative and dynamic workplace, where collaboration and support are at the core of everything we do. At our firm, you’ll have the opportunity to take on significant responsibilities, work in a flexible environment, and tackle challenging projects from the outset. Our culture is designed for ambitious professionals who want to make an immediate impact while continuing to push boundaries and achieve our greater mission. You’ll be empowered with a high level of responsibility, trust, and flexibility, providing an exciting and creative space for you to help reshape how the world views alternative investments. With competitive total rewards, performance-based bonuses, and a clear path for career growth, you’ll have everything you need to develop both now and over the longer term.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Vice President, Data Engineering to define and lead PICTON's data strategy across investment data, analytics, and AI, and to show what an AI-native data organization looks like in practice.

This is a strategic, hands-on leadership role
. You will be accountable for data across all PICTON's businesses. You'll own the architecture, governance, and engineering capabilities that turn complex financial data into reliable, accessible and actionable products for people and for AI agents. We want someone who embraces AI in their processes and who can bring that way of working across an entire team.

You will work closely with Engineering, Investment, Product, and AI teams
to build a modern data foundation that enables faster innovation and better decision-making.

What You'll Own

Data Strategy & AI-Ready Architecture

Serve as the single accountable owner for data across PICTON's businesses, setting direction, resolving competing priorities, and ensuring every business can rely on consistent, trusted data.
Define and execute PICTON's enterprise data strategy, architecture, and roadmap across Databricks, Snowflake, APIs, applications, analytics, and AI.
Own the technical build that enables PICTON's AI roadmap, working with AI and business leaders to sequence data capabilities so planned AI initiatives have the data, access, and governance they need to ship.
Design the platform so AI is a first-class consumer of data (e.g., well-governed semantic layers, rich metadata, and secure interfaces such as APIs and MCP servers that agents and LLM applications can reliably use).
Make pragmatic architecture decisions that balance performance, security, cost, and business needs, including the cost and governance of AI workloads.
Build a modern data platform supporting portfolio construction, performance, risk, analytics, and AI use cases.

AI-Accelerated Data Engineering & Governance

Lead the design of reliable, scalable pipelines for market, security, portfolio, and historical data, using AI coding assistants and agentic tools to shorten build and iteration cycles.
Apply AI to the data lifecycle itself, including automated data quality checks, anomaly detection, lineage and documentation generation, metadata enrichment, and reconciliation.
Establish practical standards for data quality, lineage, governance, security, and ownership, including guardrails for how AI tools and agents access sensitive financial data.
Evolve financial data models and semantic layers so data is consistent and reusable across products, teams, and AI systems.

Leadership, Mentorship & Culture

Build and lead a high-performing Data Engineering and Data Platform team
.
Partner with Engineering, Investment, Product, and AI leaders to translate business needs into effective data solutions.
Identify opportunities to leverage modern data and AI technologies to create competitive advantage.
Communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and business stakeholders.

What We're Looking For

10+ years of experience in data engineering, data platforms, architecture, or technology leadership, including significant team leadership experience.
Experience owning data across multiple business lines or functions, including balancing their competing needs and driving shared standards.
Experience building agentic AI solutions: designing agents and workflows that use tools, retrieve from enterprise data, and operate within clear security and governance boundaries, along with practical approaches to evaluating their accuracy and reliability.
Strong experience with modern cloud data platforms, particularly Databricks, Snowflake, SQL, APIs, and distributed data pipelines.
Deep understanding of financial and investment data, including securities, portfolios, market data, performance, risk, and time-series data.
Experience building data platforms that support analytics, applications, and AI/LLM workloads, including retrieval, semantic layers, and structured data access for models.
Strong understanding of data governance, quality, lineage, security, and ownership, and how these extend to AI systems.
Ability to move between strategic thinking and technical detail, making pragmatic architecture decisions.
Strong business acumen and exceptional communication and stakeholder-management skills.
Hands-on, current use of AI in your own workflow. You regularly use tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar to build, debug, document, and analyze, and you can give concrete examples of where it changed your speed or output.
Experience with LLM evaluation, observability, or AI cost management in production and familiarity with Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar standards for connecting AI to enterprise systems.
A track record of mentoring engineers and shaping team culture. You can point to people you've developed and to teams that took on more ownership and improved how they work under your leadership.

Our Commitment to Employees

At PICTON Investments
, we take pride in enhancing our employees' experiences through a comprehensive suite of exceptional perks and programs. Our benefits include corporate fitness reimbursement and discounts, VersaFi memberships (formerly Women in Capital Markets), Picton investment counseling and portfolio management services, volunteer and charitable donation matching, maternity and parental leave top-up, recognition awards, semi-annual performance bonuses, a generous annual vacation entitlement (minimum of 15 days per year), training and development reimbursement, extensive health and dental benefits, a healthcare spending account, and more.

These offerings are designed to support your career growth, well-being, and overall success. Join us and thrive in an environment that values and invests in you!

jobs.description:
We are pleased to be supporting Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group (“CC&L Financial Group”) in the search for a Head of Public Markets & Quant Technology
(the “Principal”). This is a newly created leadership role that will be instrumental in defining and delivering the technology strategy that supports the full public markets and quantitative investment lifecycle. Working in close partnership with investment professionals, quantitative researchers, traders, operations, risk, compliance, and finance teams, the successful candidate will modernize platforms, drive automation, improve data quality, strengthen operational resilience, and enable scalable, technology-led investment capabilities.

This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for an experienced technology executive who combines strategic vision, strong engineering expertise, and a deep understanding of investment workflows. The successful candidate will serve as the primary technology partner to Public Markets and Quant stakeholders, bringing together teams, capabilities, and priorities into a cohesive business-aligned function. The role offers significant front-office engagement, broad visibility across the organization, and the opportunity to lead a critical technology domain, influence the operating model, and serve as a strategic partner in delivering the next generation of investment technology.

Vancouver, BC or Toronto, ON (Hybrid)

About Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group

Connor, Clark & Lunn Financial Group is Canada’s largest and fastest growing privately owned asset management firm, providing a broad range of traditional and alternative investment products and services through a network of 15 affiliates and subsidiaries. With already more than $230 billion in assets under management, the organization combines the entrepreneurial strengths of its investment affiliates with the scale, operational expertise, and shared resources of a diversified enterprise.

As CC&L Financial Group continues to evolve its investment technology capabilities and operating model, the firm is seeking a senior leader to define and execute the technology strategy supporting its Public Markets and Quant businesses. This role will help shape the future of investment technology across portfolio management, research, trading, investment operations, and data capabilities, while driving modernization, automation, resilience, and measurable business outcomes.

The Opportunity

Reporting into the Co-Heads of Technology, the Principal will lead the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of technology capabilities across the public markets and quantitative investment ecosystem. This includes portfolio management, investment research, analytics, trading, investment operations, post-trade workflows, data quality, reporting, and platform resilience.

The Principal will serve as the primary technology partner to investment professionals and business stakeholders, translating business priorities into a clear technology roadmap while balancing long-term modernization objectives with practical execution. They will collaborate closely with enterprise technology teams across data, AI and automation, cloud, infrastructure, cybersecurity, service management, quality assurance, release management, and site reliability to bring enterprise-grade capabilities and standards into the public markets and quantitative investing domain.

This is not a traditional application ownership or support role. It is a business-facing technology leadership position with accountability for technology outcomes across the full investment lifecycle and an opportunity to lead meaningful transformation across a critical investment technology function.

Key Responsibilities

Define and execute the technology strategy and multi-year roadmap for Public Markets and Quant Technology, aligning investments with business priorities and organizational objectives.
Partner with portfolio managers, quantitative researchers, traders, operations, risk, compliance, and finance teams to translate business needs into scalable technology solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes.
Lead the modernization of investment platforms, processes, and architecture across front-, middle-, and back-office functions.
Oversee technology capabilities supporting portfolio management, investment research, analytics, decision-support tools, trading, order management, execution, trade capture, and post-trade workflows.
Drive automation initiatives that reduce manual effort, improve straight-through processing, strengthen controls, and enhance operational efficiency across the investment lifecycle.
Lead the evolution of quantitative and systematic investment platforms, including research-to-production workflows and technology capabilities supporting quantitative investing.
Establish and champion modern engineering practices, including cloud adoption, APIs, CI/CD, DevSecOps, observability, automated testing, data validation, production telemetry, and site reliability principles.
Improve platform resilience, operational risk management, service quality, production support practices, and incident reduction through proactive monitoring and continuous improvement.
Oversee investment data foundations, including market data, reference data, security master capabilities, data quality, lineage, governance, and controls.
Partner with enterprise technology teams across data, AI and automation, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud services, service management, quality assurance, and release management to leverage shared capabilities and standards.
Lead and develop a high-performing multidisciplinary team of engineers, analysts, product owners, technology specialists, support professionals, and domain experts, helping shape team structure, operating practices, and capabilities as the organization continues to evolve its business-aligned technology model.
Simplify complexity across technology and operating environments while improving data quality, governance, scalability, and organizational effectiveness.

Skills and Qualifications

Extensive experience leading technology organizations within investment management, asset management, hedge funds, capital markets, trading technology, or broader financial services environments.
Strong understanding of front-to-back investment workflows, including portfolio management, trading, positions, P&L, risk, settlement, reconciliation, reporting, data flows, and operational processes supporting investment management.
Demonstrated track record leading technology transformation and modernization initiatives within complex, regulated, or high-scale environments, including platform modernization, architecture simplification, automation, data strategy, resiliency improvements, and operating model evolution.
Strong engineering leadership and technical credibility, with the ability to influence architecture decisions, challenge technical approaches, engage senior engineering teams, and drive operational excellence.
Exposure to platforms such as OMS, EMS, PMS, IBOR, ABOR, risk, performance, reconciliation, fund accounting, market data, or investment data solutions is considered valuable.
Experience with quantitative or systematic investing technology and research-to-production investment platforms is considered an asset.
Exceptional stakeholder management skills, with a proven ability to build credibility and partner effectively across investment, operations, risk, compliance, finance, technology, and executive leadership teams.
Demonstrated success building and leading high-performing multidisciplinary teams across engineering, product, operations, support, and vendor management functions.
Ability to balance strategic thinking with practical execution, bringing sound judgment, strong leadership presence, and a focus on measurable business outcomes.

Computer Vision

Dayforce is a global human capital management (HCM) company headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, with operations across North America, Europe, Middle East, Africa (EMEA), and the Asia Pacific Japan (APJ) region.

Our award-winning Cloud HCM platform offers a unified solution database and continuous calculation engine, driving efficiency, productivity and compliance for the global workforce.

Our brand promise - Makes Work Life Better™ - Reflects our commitment to employees, customers, partners and communities globally.

We are seeking an experienced and visionary Sr. Director, Enterprise Data and AI Platform to define and execute the strategy, architecture, and delivery of Dayforce's enterprise data, AI, and contextual intelligence capabilities. This leader will drive the evolution of our modern data ecosystem, enabling trusted, scalable, and AI-ready data solutions that support business functions across Sales, Marketing, Finance, HR, Customer Success, Support, Services, Legal, and other enterprise organizations.

As part of this transformation, the role will lead the strategy and implementation of the Enterprise Agentic AI Platform, enabling employees to interact with enterprise data through secure, AI-powered conversational experiences that complement and, over time, transform traditional dashboards and reporting.

The successful candidate will lead a global organization of data, AI platform, and engineering professionals, including managers, direct reports, and external partners. This highly strategic yet hands-on leadership role requires deep technical expertise, strong architectural vision, exceptional cross-functional leadership, and a passion for delivering innovative, AI-driven solutions that accelerate business outcomes.

Evaluate emerging AI technologies and establish enterprise AI architecture, governance, and security standards.

Governance, Security & Architecture

TVO Media Education Group (TVO) is devoted to inspiring learning that changes lives and enriches communities. We are an internationally recognized digital learning organization that strives to engage, inform, and educate Ontarians of all ages.

Who We Are

We are an agency of the Ontario Ministry of Education and a registered charity that contributes to learning, civic engagement, and public service media across Ontario. We provide free, trusted, and accessible educational content that can support Ontarians of all ages, regardless of background, location, or circumstance. To fulfill our mandate, TVO delivers curriculum-connected resources through TVO Learn and TVOkids, offers Ontario’s largest online high school through TVO ILC, and produces journalism, documentaries, current affairs programming, and podcasts with TVO Today that help Ontarians understand the issues shaping their communities.

What We’re Looking For

TVO’s purpose is to inspire learning that changes lives and enriches communities. Our mission is to create engaging learning experiences for all through quality content, services, and technology. To realize our vision of becoming a globally recognized digital learning organization, we must continually reimagine how learning experiences are designed and delivered.

Artificial intelligence is reshaping education, from assessment and academic integrity to learner pathways, instructional practice, and support. These changes create extraordinary opportunities while raising important questions about equity, accessibility, ethics, and educational quality. TVO has an opportunity to help lead this transformation.

The Director, Education Design & Intelligence will shape how TVO responds. Working across TVOkids, TVO Learn, Mathify, TVO ILC, and emerging lifelong learning initiatives, this leader will guide TVO Education’s approach to AI, advance future-focused learning design, build staff capability, and ensure our learning experiences remain relevant, inclusive, and impactful. This is the opportunity to help TVO Education design what learning becomes next.

The Role

Reporting to the Vice President, Education, the Director, Education Design & Intelligence leads TVO’s Learning Experience Design and Production functions, with direct accountability for the Manager, Learning Experience Design and the Production Manager.

The Director works in close partnership with the Director, Curriculum & Course Production, Director, Content Engagement, and Director, Academic Services. Together, the Directors bring complementary expertise to the design and delivery of TVO’s education portfolio. The Director, Education Design & Intelligence contributes specialized leadership in learning design, AI integration, emerging technology, professional learning, and production.

Operating at the intersection of learning science, educational design, artificial intelligence, and digital innovation, the Director translates emerging developments into practical strategies, standards, and learning experiences that strengthen learner outcomes and organizational capability.

How You Will Make An Impact

Learning Design, Pathways & Assessment

Lead the human-centred design and continuous improvement of learning experiences across TVO’s education portfolio, ensuring they are inclusive, accessible, pedagogically grounded, and responsive to changing learner needs.
Establish and maintain shared learning design principles, standards, and frameworks that guide how educational experiences are conceived, developed, evaluated, and improved across programs and platforms.
Work in close partnership with the Director, Curriculum & Course Production, Director, Content Engagement, and Director, Academic Services to strengthen learner journeys, pathways, engagement, and educational outcomes.
Lead the continuous review and modernization of assessment and evaluation practices across TVO Education, responding to developments in AI, academic integrity, learner evidence, and emerging approaches to teaching and learning.
Establish processes for regularly evaluating learning design standards, assessment approaches, and learner journeys, using research, learner feedback, outcomes data, prototyping, and testing to guide continuous improvement.
Examine how AI and emerging technologies are reshaping curriculum, instruction, assessment, learner supports, credentialing, and progression, and translate those developments into practical opportunities for TVO.
Embed collaborative design practices that centre diverse perspectives, lived experiences, accessibility, and learner needs.

AI Strategy, Emerging Technology & Professional Learning

Develop and lead TVO Education’s AI in Education strategy, guiding principles, and implementation roadmap.
Establish responsible, ethical, equitable, accessible, and learner-centred approaches to integrating AI into educational experiences, services, and internal workflows.
Work closely with the Vice President, Education, the Chief Technology Officer, and technology teams to align AI and educational priorities with platform development, system integration, technology roadmaps, data governance, privacy, and security requirements.
Identify, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, tools, platforms, and practices that can advance TVO’s educational mission and improve learning experiences.
Provide timely advice to Education leaders on the educational opportunities, risks, and implications of AI and other disruptive technologies.
Develop and implement a professional learning strategy that builds AI literacy, digital fluency, instructional capability, and confidence across the Education division.
Create learning experiences, communities of practice, guidance, and resources that help employees use emerging technologies effectively, critically, creatively, and responsibly.
Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning that enables teams to navigate educational and technological change.
Contribute expertise to the development of AI literacy and fluency initiatives for educators, learners, and families in collaboration with the Directors responsible for programming, content, and academic services.

Learning Experience Design & Production Leadership

Provide direct leadership and strategic direction to the Manager, Learning Experience Design and the Production Manager, developing a cohesive, high-performing, and multidisciplinary team.
Ensure Learning Experience Design and Production operate as an integrated, multifunctional team supporting programming priorities across the Education division.
Work with Directors and program teams to translate educational priorities into clear scopes, design approaches, production plans, and high-quality learner experiences.
Establish effective operating models, standards, processes, and workflows that support quality, consistency, accessibility, efficiency, innovation, and accountability.
Oversee the delivery of educational experiences and digital learning assets, ensuring work is completed to agreed standards, timelines, and program requirements.
Balance portfolio-wide priorities and deploy design and production capacity where it can create the greatest learner and organizational impact.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, creating clarity, encouraging collaboration, and building the capabilities needed for future-focused educational design and production.
Manage budgets, contracts, technology investments, and resources associated with Learning Experience Design and Production, and oversee allocated resources for professional learning and innovation initiatives in AI and emerging educational technology.

Cross-Portfolio Leadership, Collaboration & Sector Engagement

Serve as a fully integrated member of the Education leadership team, contributing to divisional strategy, planning, priority setting, and decision-making.
Work in close partnership with Directors across Education to ensure that learning design, AI, production, technology, and learner experience decisions support shared educational priorities.
Build strong working relationships across TVO so that educational design and AI initiatives are aligned with broader organizational, technology, research, communications, and operational directions.
Represent TVO in provincial, national, and international conversations about AI in Education, learning design, assessment, emerging technology, and the future of learning.
Develop relationships with educational institutions, researchers, government, technology organizations, and innovation networks that can contribute expertise, evidence, or capabilities to TVO’s work.
Identify and help advance appropriate opportunities for research, pilots, technology integration, and collaboration that support TVO’s educational priorities.
Bring emerging research, sector developments, and external perspectives into TVO to inform strategy, program design, professional learning, and continuous improvement.

What is the Opportunity?

As part of the Group Risk Management team, the Director, Counterparty Credit Risk Analytics leads a team which is responsible for the conceptual design, development, and ongoing maintenance of the mathematical models used for the measurement and capitalization of the counterparty credit risk of RBC's derivative and SFT portfolio. This includes ensuring that the model's underlying methodologies are appropriate and that they are implemented with integrity, to facilitate the effective management of the bank's CCR.

What will you do?

Work with model users to understand their business requirements.
Conduct research, review regulatory requirements and consult with industry stakeholders to evaluate best practices for modeling.
Make recommendations on model methodologies, and develop technical implementation, either for production usage or to serve as a prototype for benchmark testing.
Provide business requirements with technical implementation details and user acceptance criteria to technology teams for production deployment, and validate implementation using independently developed benchmark models.
Document model methodologies, implementation details and testing results, and work with internal validation to facilitate their approval of the models.
Develop tools to assess and monitor model performance, including assumptions and limitations, on an ongoing basis for reporting to the various model monitoring governance committees.
Investigate and remediate modeling issues identified through regular re-reviews, ongoing monitoring or by internal validation.
Recalibrate models on a regular basis.
Re-assessment and testing of models, including assumptions and limitations and benchmarking against alternative models, and documentation of the results in models whitepapers and annual assessments for review by internal validation.

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Digital Marketing Director you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

high-performance, people-focused culture

Job Summary

This fast-paced role is ideal for someone who thrives on identifying and remediating operational risk challenges with a focus on the investment environment. Reporting to the Senior Director, the Associate Director will help evolve HOOPP's Operational Risk Management (ORM) and Enterprise Crisis and Continuity (ECC) programs by promoting a strong risk culture and partnering with business areas across the organization to identify and mitigate key operational risks.

The role will support both programs. For Operational Risk, the Associate Director will support the execution and enhancement of HOOPP's ORM programs including vendor risk management, operational risk event reporting, key risk indicators and industry event surveillance. This role will also work directly with front office trading teams to review end-to-end processes and surface risks, inefficiencies and control gaps. For designated divisions, support the Operational Risk Management (ORM) and Enterprise Crisis and Continuity programs.

Investment Management:
Partner with front office trading teams to review end-to-end processes, identify operational risks, inefficiencies, control gaps and opportunities for improvement.

Vendor Risk Management
Operational Risk Event reporting
Key Risk Indicators
Industry Event surveillance and reporting

Facilitate business impact analyses (BIAs), dependency mapping, and risk assessments in collaboration with divisions and IT partners.
Support enterprise response, recovery, and restoration activities during actual crisis or disruption events.
Contribute to the ongoing evolution of the Crisis Management program and support the implementation and awareness for leaders, plan owners, and staff.
Provide advisory support to business units on crisis preparedness, continuity planning, and resilience best practices.

Identify opportunities to use technology, automation and AI to improve efficiency, decision-making and control effectiveness.
Support the design, testing and implementation of tools that reduce manual activity, improve data quality and enhance the user experience.
Develop and leverage AI to automate manual processes, which can include ongoing monitoring activities, data extraction and report generation.

University education with a degree in business, risk management, or other relevant major.
8+ years of progressive risk management experience, in asset management, pension or financial services industries. Previous pension fund experience is an asset.

Excellent written and oral communication skills.

Demonstrated strong research, innovation, and problem-solving skills.
Motivated self-starter that can work in a fast-paced and high-performance culture
Alignment with HOOPP's values.

Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

As part of the Group Risk Management team, the Director, Counterparty Credit Risk Analytics leads a team which is responsible for the conceptual design, development, and ongoing maintenance of the mathematical models used for the measurement and capitalization of the counterparty credit risk of RBC's derivative and SFT portfolio. This includes ensuring that the model's underlying methodologies are appropriate and that they are implemented with integrity, to facilitate the effective management of the bank's CCR.

Work with model users to understand their business requirements.
Conduct research, review regulatory requirements and consult with industry stakeholders to evaluate best practices for modeling.
Make recommendations on model methodologies, and develop technical implementation, either for production usage or to serve as a prototype for benchmark testing.

Document model methodologies, implementation details and testing results, and work with internal validation to facilitate their approval of the models.
Develop tools to assess and monitor model performance, including assumptions and limitations, on an ongoing basis for reporting to the various model monitoring governance committees.
Investigate and remediate modeling issues identified through regular re-reviews, ongoing monitoring or by internal validation.

Re-assessment and testing of models, including assumptions and limitations and benchmarking against alternative models, and documentation of the results in models whitepapers and annual assessments for review by internal validation.

Broad knowledge of traded products across various asset classes.
